en.name: Coffee beans, whole
en.summary: Whole roasted coffee beans keep 3–5 months from purchase and 3–5 months after opening in a cool, dark, airtight container, or 3–4 months in the fridge once opened. Unlike ground coffee, the whole bean keeps as well opened as sealed — the intact bean is doing the protecting.
en.pantry: 3–5 months from purchase, and the same 3–5 months after opening, in an airtight opaque container somewhere cool, dark and dry. That the two figures match is the whole argument for buying beans rather than grounds: the roasted bean holds its aromatics inside a solid structure, so opening the bag does not start a fast clock the way grinding does. Coffee does not spoil, it stales — an old bean makes a dull, papery cup, not an unsafe one. Keep the tin away from the kettle and off any sunny shelf.
en.fridge: 3–4 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below after opening, in a container that genuinely seals. Cold slows the oils in the bean from oxidising, but the fridge is humid and full of smells, and roasted coffee absorbs both. If you cannot seal it properly, the cupboard figure is longer anyway, which makes the fridge the weaker option for most kitchens rather than the obvious upgrade.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for whole beans. Freezing is widely practised and does no harm if the beans are sealed airtight and taken out in single portions, but there is no published figure to quote here, so treat it as practice rather than a documented limit. The one thing to avoid is repeatedly taking a bag in and out, which condenses moisture onto the beans each time.
en.thawing: Let a frozen portion come to room temperature inside its sealed container before opening, so that condensation lands on the container rather than on the beans. Grind only after it has warmed.
spoilage: A flat, papery or cardboard smell instead of a roasted, sweet one.
Beans that look dull and dry when they used to be glossy, or vice versa — oily beans going sticky.
A sour, ashy cup from beans that used to taste good.
A musty smell or mould in beans that were stored damp.
tips: Buy beans rather than grounds; they keep as well opened as they do sealed.
Grind per brew and store the rest whole.
Use an opaque airtight tin, not a clear jar in the light.
If you freeze, do it in single-use portions and never return a portion to the freezer.

faq.q: How long do coffee beans keep?
faq.a: 3–5 months from purchase and 3–5 months after opening in an airtight container in a cool cupboard, or 3–4 months in the fridge after opening.

faq.q: Should coffee beans be kept in the fridge?
faq.a: Only if the container seals properly. The cupboard figure is actually longer, and the fridge is humid and full of odours that coffee absorbs.
They stale rather than spoil. An old bean gives a flat, papery cup but is not unsafe. Mould only appears if the beans got genuinely damp.

zh.name: 咖啡豆
zh.summary: 整顆烘焙咖啡豆自購買日起 3～5 個月，開封後同樣是 3～5 個月，前提是陰涼、避光、氣密；開封後冷藏則是 3～4 個月。和咖啡粉不同，整顆豆子開封後和未開封一樣耐放——保護它的就是那顆完整的豆子本身。
zh.pantry: 不透光的氣密容器，放陰涼、避光、乾燥處，自購買日起 3～5 個月，開封後同樣 3～5 個月。這兩個數字一樣，就是「買豆不買粉」最完整的論證：烘焙好的豆子把香氣鎖在一個結實的結構裡，所以拆封並不會像研磨那樣立刻啟動一個快轉的時鐘。咖啡不會腐敗，它是走味——老豆子沖出來是沉悶帶紙味的一杯，而不是不安全的一杯。鐵罐請遠離熱水壺，也別放在有陽光的層架上。
zh.fridge: 開封後放進真正密得起來的容器、冷藏 4 °C 以下，3～4 個月。低溫會拖慢豆子裡油脂氧化，但冰箱又潮濕、味道又多，而烘焙咖啡兩樣都吸。如果沒辦法確實密封，反正櫥櫃的數字還比較長——所以對多數廚房來說，冰箱在這裡是比較弱的選項，而不是理所當然的升級。
zh.freezer: 整顆咖啡豆沒有公布的冷凍期限。冷凍是很普遍的做法，只要密封確實、而且一次只取一份，也不會有害；但這裡沒有公開數字可以引用，所以請當成做法而不是有憑有據的上限。唯一要避免的是把同一包反覆進出冷凍庫，每一次都會讓水氣凝在豆子上。
zh.thawing: 讓小份維持密封回到室溫再打開，讓結露留在容器上而不是豆子上。回溫之後才研磨。
spoilage: 聞起來平板、有紙味或紙板味，而不是烘焙的甜香。
本來油亮的豆子變得乾啞，或反過來——出油的豆子變得黏手。
本來好喝的豆子沖出來發酸、有灰味。
受潮存放的豆子出現霉味或發霉。
tips: 買豆不買粉；豆子開封後和未開封一樣耐放。
要沖多少磨多少，其餘維持整顆保存。
用不透光的氣密鐵罐，不要用透明罐放在光下。
要冷凍就分成單次份量，而且取出過的那一份不要再放回去。

faq.a: 氣密容器放陰涼櫥櫃，自購買日起 3～5 個月，開封後同樣 3～5 個月；開封後冷藏 3～4 個月。
只有在容器真的密得起來時才值得。櫥櫃的數字其實比較長，而冰箱潮濕又有味道，咖啡全都會吸。
它是走味不是腐敗。老豆子沖出來平板帶紙味，但不危險。只有真的受潮才會長霉。
